The scouting brief

Who handles the closing overs?

The dashboard ranks batting and bowling contributions in the final 25% of a scheduled T20 innings, then compares those numbers with the player's earlier-innings baseline.
Primary window · final 25%

Batting shortlist

Ranked by a balanced pressure-performance score. Strike rate is shown for context.

Bowling shortlist

Ranked by economy, wicket-taking, improvement and dot-ball contribution.
How to read this: a high pressure strike rate is not enough on its own. The ranking also considers average, dismissal control, exposure and improvement over the player's baseline. Bowling uses the reverse direction for economy: fewer runs conceded is better.

Behind the numbers

Method, scope & limitations

A short explanation of what was measured, what was checked and where the source data does not allow stronger claims.
01

Define pressure

Pressure is the final 25% of the scheduled innings quota. In a full 20-over innings this is overs 16–20. Shortened quotas use their revised allocation.

02

Build a baseline

Earlier-innings performance is used as a comparison, so a player's late-innings number is not read in isolation.

03

Adjust for exposure

Minimum pressure-ball and match exposure rules reduce the influence of tiny samples. Shrinkage moderates unstable rates.

Batting score

A composite of pressure strike rate, pressure average, strike-rate lift over baseline and dismissal control. Higher is better. Strike rate and average are not treated as the same thing.

Bowling score

A composite of pressure economy, pressure wicket rate, economy improvement over baseline and dot-ball percentage. Lower economy is better; wicket and dot-ball rates reward positive outcomes.

Data quality checks

Pressure-window sensitivity

Changing the definition changes the shortlist. This is a real limitation and should be disclosed.
WindowPressure shareTop battersTop bowlers
Important limitations: 16 selected matches have no ball-by-ball coverage. Some extras are ambiguous; one impossible over was excluded from bowling calculations. The supplied data does not provide complete targets and innings totals for every match, so this dashboard does not claim to calculate required-run-rate pressure or reproduce every official scorecard. Economy values should be read as dataset-derived estimates, not official career statistics.

Source and reproducibility

All values shown here are loaded from the final analysis CSVs produced from the official competition data pack. The full project ZIP includes source files, analysis code, validation tables, sensitivity tests and the written methodology report.

This is a self-contained dashboard: it does not call an external API or fetch live statistics. Save this HTML file and open it in a modern browser to use it offline.
